steps.title: free heap memory
steps.explanation:
`free(p)` frees heap memory, but does not clear the pointer variable itself.

Be careful because `p` may become dangling after release.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Key point: malloc/free are used in a 1:1 ratio.

quiz.question: What happens if you free() the address of a stack variable (local variable)?
quiz.explanation:
`free` can only process addresses allocated with `malloc/calloc/realloc`.
 If you enter an incorrect address, the memory manager will become confused and force the program to terminate.

misconceptions.wrong: When you free(p), the p variable itself disappears.
misconceptions.correct: The p variable remains the same.
misconceptions.why:
It's just that the 'house' pointed to by p has been demolished.
p still holds the address of the demolished house (Dangling Pointer).

keyTakeaway: Be sure to repay what you borrow `freely`. `malloc` and `free` are a pair.
